title: Identification and characterisation of an elusive bacterial enzyme system for chloromethane dehalogenation
task: Identify and characterize bacterial corrinoid-dependent dehalogenase system for chloromethane degradation
key_results: Cdm system identified in Acetobacterium dehalogenans via comparative transcriptomics; CdmB structure reveals hydrophobic channeling to cobalamin-dependent active site; homologs found across Bacillota and Asgardarchaeota phyla
comments: The discovery of a distinct cobalamin-dependent system separate from the characterized Cmu pathway is significant for environmental microbiology, though in vitro turnover kinetics and substrate scope quantification are not detailed.

hypotheses.hypothesis: A distinct corrinoid-dependent methyltransferase (Cdm) system mediates chloromethane dehalogenation in anaerobic acetogens
hypotheses.result: cdmBCA cluster identified and biochemically characterized; CdmB structure shows haloalkane-specific substrate channeling

hypotheses.hypothesis: The Cdm system has broader substrate range than O-demethylases but narrower than aerobic Cmu systems
hypotheses.result: Cdm reacts with haloalkanes but not methoxylated aromatics, distinguishing it from related enzymes

title: Event-based spatiotemporal networks for modelling emergent phenomena in complex systems
task: Model emergent spatiotemporal dynamics in complex systems via event-based network framework
key_results: Framework enables fine-grained tracking of COVID-19 transmission routes, superspreader identification, and delay propagation in public transportation networks
comments: The event-centric abstraction is powerful for bridging scales but relies heavily on sufficient event resolution; applicability to developmental biology and ecology is promising but largely prospective.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Event-based spatiotemporal networks can recover macroscopic dynamics from fine-grained micro-level processes across scales
hypotheses.result: Successfully tracked infection patterns and identified superspreaders in respiratory pathogen outbreak; modeled delay propagation in public transit

title: One-site polarity switch enhances catalytic efficiency and stability of d-allulose 3-epimerase via flexibility–rigidity rebalancing
task: Elucidate mechanism of enhanced catalytic efficiency via single amino acid substitution in d-allulose 3-epimerase
key_results: E35H mutation increases catalytic efficiency 1.4-fold (Km reduction 1.3-fold, kcat elevation 1.1-fold); melting temperature increased from 92.6°C to 94.3°C
comments: The flexibility-rigidity rebalancing model is convincing, but the modest kcat improvement suggests substrate turnover is not fully optimized by this single mutation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: E35H substitution reduces local hydrogen bonding and increases active site flexibility while stabilizing the protein scaffold
hypotheses.result: RMSF analysis shows increased flexibility at residues 35 and 6; decreased global fluctuations; hydrogen bonds at position 35 reduced from six to five

hypotheses.hypothesis: E152-substrate O1 interaction provides additional anchoring in the E35H variant
hypotheses.result: Novel interaction identified in structural analysis contributing to improved catalysis

title: Partial fluidization theory of collective cell migration
task: Model viscoelastic behavior and solid-liquid coexistence in migrating cell monolayers
key_results: Partial fluidization framework captures plug flow in microfluidic channels, spatial coexistence of mobile and immobile domains, and rotational flow in circular chambers
comments: The continuous transition via fluidization order parameter elegantly unifies disparate mechanical behaviors, though validation on 3D tissues and curved/compliant substrates remains outstanding.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cell monolayers exhibit tunable solid-liquid coexistence controlled by shear stress
hypotheses.result: Model successfully reproduces experimental observations of plug flow, spatial domain coexistence, and rotational flow

title: Reversible alterations of brain acetate metabolism associated with alcohol consumption
task: Characterize reversible brain acetate metabolism alterations across alcohol use spectrum
key_results: Heavy drinkers and AUD patients showed elevated cerebral metabolic rate for acetate (CMRAc) compared to light drinkers; AUDTx at 1 week abstinence showed lower CMRAc (p=0.007); CMRAc normalized after 1 month abstinence to light drinker levels
comments: The normalization of acetate oxidation within weeks of abstinence is encouraging for AUD reversibility, though the functional significance of elevated CMRAc remains incompletely characterized.

model_io.model: Human subjects (Light Drinkers, Heavy Drinkers, AUD recovery, AUD treatment-seekers) with [2-13C]acetate-MRS

hypotheses.hypothesis: Chronic alcohol use elevates brain acetate oxidation capacity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; heavy drinkers showed elevated CMRAc vs. light drinkers

hypotheses.hypothesis: Early AUD abstinence reduces CMRAc; prolonged abstinence normalizes it
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; AUDTx showed lower CMRAc at 1 week, normalized by 1 month

title: Specifically targeted engineered exosomes loaded with circAKR1A1 enhance tumorigenesis and metastasis in prostate cancer by activating the PI3K/Akt signalling pathway
task: Assess targeted engineered exosomes delivering circAKR1A1 in bone metastatic prostate cancer
key_results: circAKR1A1 expression correlated with prostate cancer metastasis; OE-circAKR1A1-exosomes specifically targeted bone microenvironment cells; activated PI3K/Akt signaling, facilitating invasion and metastasis
comments: The proof-of-concept for targeted exosome delivery is solid, but the endogenous function of circAKR1A1 in non-metastatic disease remains unclear.

model_io.model: Bone metastatic prostate cancer cell lines with targeted engineered exosomes

hypotheses.hypothesis: circAKR1A1 delivered via targeted exosomes activates PI3K/Akt to promote invasion and metastasis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; OE-circAKR1A1-exosomes activated PI3K/Akt and enhanced metastatic phenotype

title: Tipping the balance: NRF2’s dual role in ferroptotic fate
task: Resolve dual role of NRF2 in ferroptosis regulation and cancer chemoresistance
key_results: NRF2 sustained activation enhances antioxidant defenses and detoxification; NRF2 also orchestrates ferroptosis-related genes (glutathione biosynthesis, lipid metabolism, iron homeostasis); context-dependent effects vary by cell type and metabolic state
comments: This review synthesizes emerging evidence for NRF2-ferroptosis crosstalk, but the determinants of context-dependent outcomes (pro-survival vs. ferroptosis-promoting) require further mechanistic clarification.

hypotheses.hypothesis: NRF2 drives chemoresistance through sustained activation of antioxidant/detoxification pathways
hypotheses.result: Established; NRF2 is recognized as key driver of drug resistance

hypotheses.hypothesis: NRF2 also regulates ferroptosis susceptibility through modulation of glutathione, lipid metabolism, and iron homeostasis
hypotheses.result: Emerging; context-dependent effects suggest paradoxical pro-ferroptosis roles under specific conditions

title: USP24-dependent STAT2 stabilization mediates physiologic and pathologic bone formation
task: Determine USP24-STAT2 axis in bone formation regulation
key_results: USP24 stabilizes STAT2 via deubiquitination; USP24 silencing in FOP mouse model markedly reduced heterotopic ossification; loss of USP24 reduced osteoblast differentiation by ~50%
comments: The dual role in both physiologic and pathologic bone formation makes USP24-STAT2 an attractive but complex therapeutic target.

model_io.model: Primary osteoblasts and FOP mouse model

hypotheses.hypothesis: USP24 deubiquitinates and stabilizes STAT2 to promote osteogenesis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; USP24 loss reduced STAT2 protein and impaired osteoblast differentiation

hypotheses.hypothesis: USP24-STAT2 pathway drives pathologic bone formation in FOP
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; rAAV-mediated Usp24 silencing diminished HO pathogenesis

title: YTHDC1 drives senescence evasion in ovarian cancer through m6A-mediated TERT stabilization
task: Resolve YTHDC1-m6A-TERT axis in ovarian cancer senescence evasion
key_results: YTHDC1 (m6A reader) elevated in advanced-stage ovarian cancer and correlated with poor survival; YTHDC1 ablation induced proliferative arrest and senescence; YTHDC1 recognizes m6A-modified TERT transcripts to stabilize telomerase mRNA
comments: The epitranscriptomic mechanism linking m6A reading to telomerase maintenance is novel, and the sensitivity of YTHDC1-knockdown cells to senolytic ABT-263 has immediate clinical implications.

model_io.model: Ovarian cancer cell lines and patient tumors with YTHDC1 ablation

hypotheses.hypothesis: YTHDC1 recognition of m6A-modified TERT stabilizes telomerase mRNA and maintains telomere homeostasis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; YTHDC1 knockdown reduced TERT mRNA stability and triggered telomere shortening

hypotheses.hypothesis: YTHDC1-dependent telomerase maintenance drives senescence evasion in ovarian cancer
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; YTHDC1 ablation induced senescence that was reversed by TERT restoration

title: USP33 alleviates FIS1-dependent mitochondrial fission and cardiac microvascular injury in diabetic cardiomyopathy via deubiquitinating and stabilizing ATG7
task: Define USP33-ATG7-FIS1 axis in diabetic cardiomyopathy-associated endothelial dysfunction
key_results: USP33 stabilizes ATG7 by blocking K63-linked ubiquitination, promoting lysosomal degradation of FIS1; USP33 silencing elevated FIS1, increased mitochondrial fission, and worsened endothelial dysfunction in DCM
comments: The multi-step cascade (USP33→ATG7→FIS1 autophagy) is mechanistically elegant but therapeutic targeting at which step remains unclear.

model_io.model: Endothelial cells from diabetic cardiomyopathy models

hypotheses.hypothesis: USP33 stabilizes ATG7, promoting FIS1 degradation and limiting mitochondrial fission
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; USP33 depletion elevated FIS1 and increased fission in endothelial cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: Excessive mitochondrial fission contributes to DCM-associated endothelial dysfunction
hypotheses.result: Supported; USP33 loss worsened endothelial and cardiovascular dysfunction

title: Targeted silencing of CLYBL with platelet-mimetic siRNA nanoparticles drives itaconate–mediated macrophage reprogramming and protects against sepsis-triggered lung cell death
task: Target CLYBL-itaconate pathway to reduce sepsis-induced lung injury via macrophage reprogramming
key_results: CLYBL upregulated in sepsis lung and macrophages; CLYBL silencing via platelet-mimetic siRNA nanoparticles accumulated itaconate, limited M1 polarization, preserved alveolar integrity, and reduced cell death; improved pulmonary repair without systemic toxicity
comments: The platelet-derived EV coating for siRNA delivery is clinically elegant, and the itaconate-mediated immune resolution axis is therapeutically promising.

model_io.model: Murine cecal ligation puncture (CLP) sepsis model + PEVs@PLGA-CLYBL-siRNA

hypotheses.hypothesis: CLYBL silencing elevates itaconate and reprograms macrophages toward resolution phenotype
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; CLYBL knockdown accumulated itaconate and limited M1 polarization

hypotheses.hypothesis: Platelet-mimetic nanoparticles enable efficient CLYBL-siRNA delivery with reduced toxicity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; PEVs@PLGA achieved robust knockdown and negligible systemic toxicity

title: BCL2 inhibition in acute and chronic pancreatitis — is there a therapeutic perspective?
task: Assess BCL2 inhibition as therapeutic strategy in acute vs. chronic pancreatitis
key_results: In AP models, Venetoclax redirected cell death from necrosis to apoptosis, preserving ATP and reducing inflammation without toxicity to healthy acinar cells; in CP, BCL2 inhibition showed no benefit and may exacerbate fibrogenesis
comments: The disease-context-dependent efficacy is informative for clinical translation but highlights the need for patient stratification.

model_io.model: Pancreatic acinar cell models (AP and CP contexts)

hypotheses.hypothesis: BCL2 inhibition redirects cell death from necrosis to apoptosis in AP, reducing damage
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; Venetoclax shifted death mode and reduced inflammatory markers in AP models

hypotheses.hypothesis: BCL2 inhibition provides therapeutic benefit in CP
hypotheses.result: Rejected; no benefit observed and potential exacerbation of fibrogenesis in CP context

title: Non-decameric NLRP3 reveals a TGN/MTOC-distal pathway of inflammasome activation
task: Delineate decameric vs. non-decameric NLRP3 inflammasome activation pathways
key_results: Nigericin triggers two distinct NLRP3 activation pathways: (i) rapid decameric cage-dependent (TGN/MTOC-proximal); (ii) slow-reacting non-decameric pathway (TGN/MTOC-distal); human neutrophils preferentially employ non-decameric route
comments: The spatial and kinetic distinction between two parallel pathways is mechanistically insightful and suggests cell-type-specific inflammasome assembly.

model_io.model: THP-1 macrophages, human macrophages, and human neutrophils with NLRP3 exon 3 deletion variant

hypotheses.hypothesis: Two distinct NLRP3 activation pathways exist: decameric cage-dependent and non-decameric cage-independent
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; nigericin triggers both pathways with distinct spatial and kinetic properties

hypotheses.hypothesis: Human neutrophils predominantly utilize non-decameric pathway
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; neutrophils showed preferential engagement of slow non-decameric route

title: COXFA4L2 upregulation preserves residual cytochrome c oxidase activity in COXFA4-related Leigh-like encephalopathy
task: Identify compensatory mechanisms in COXFA4-deficient mitochondria
key_results: COXFA4L2 upregulation preserves residual COX activity in patient fibroblasts despite complete loss of COXFA4 protein; 13 individuals with biallelic COXFA4 variants identified
comments: Paralog compensation may explain the milder-than-expected phenotype and suggests therapeutic intervention targets.

hypotheses.hypothesis: COXFA4L2 paralog compensates for COXFA4 loss
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; upregulation of COXFA4L2 preserves residual COX function

title: Mitochondrial RNA degradation regulates differentiation, stemness, and immune sensitivity in acute myeloid leukemia
task: Determine mitochondrial RNA degradation role in AML differentiation and immune sensitivity
key_results: mtRNA degradation increased in AML and stem cells; SUV3/PNPase degradosome upregulated in AML; depleting SUV3/PNPase accumulated mtRNA dsRNA, activated IFN-I signaling, induced differentiation and decreased stemness
comments: The coupling of mtRNA turnover to innate immune activation is elegant and suggests intrinsic mitochondrial dsRNA as a PAMP in AML.

model_io.model: AML cell lines and primary AML stem cells with SUV3/PNPase depletion

hypotheses.hypothesis: SUV3/PNPase degradation of mtRNA prevents dsRNA accumulation and innate immune activation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; SUV3/PNPase depletion caused dsRNA accumulation and IFN-I signaling

hypotheses.hypothesis: mtRNA-derived dsRNA activation of IFN-I signaling induces AML differentiation and immune sensitization
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; dsRNA accumulation triggered differentiation and increased immune-mediated cytotoxicity

title: Brieflow: an integrated computational pipeline for high-throughput analysis of optical pooled screening data
task: Develop computational pipeline for high-throughput optical pooled screening data analysis
key_results: Brieflow pipeline processed >70 million cells from 5072-gene CRISPR screen; recovered 24 distinct phenotypic clusters; MozzareLLM framework identified five core mitochondrial sub-programs missed by original analysis
comments: The integration of machine learning for phenotypic interpretation is innovative, though the biological validation of newly identified modules remains outstanding.

model_io.model: Brieflow computational pipeline with hyperplexed CRISPR-OPS data

title: The spatial proteome of the Plasmodium falciparum schizont illuminates the composition and evolutionary trajectories of its organelles
task: Map spatial proteome of P. falciparum schizont to resolve organellar composition and evolution
key_results: hyperLOPIT analysis of ~3000 P. falciparum proteins resolved 24 distinct cellular niches; classified 1646 proteins into compartments including exported sites; comparative genomics revealed spatial evolutionary patterns
comments: This is an exceptional resource for parasite cell biology, though functional validation of uncharacterized organellar proteins will require complementary approaches.

model_io.model: P. falciparum late schizont stages with hyperLOPIT spatial proteomics

title: Two Plasmodium vivax hypnozoite-expressed RNA-binding proteins inhibit liver stage replication
task: Identify hypnozoite-expressed RNA-binding proteins suppressing liver stage replication
key_results: Two hypnozoite-expressed transcripts encode putative RNA-binding proteins (IESI-1 and IESI-2); expression of each in P. yoelii blocked schizogony with parasites remaining small and uninucleate; screen revealed distinct RNA motif enrichment
comments: Functional validation in non-hypnozoite-forming species is clever but activation mechanisms of these proteins in dormancy remain to be characterized.

model_io.model: P. vivax hypnozoites and P. yoelii transgenic liver stage parasites

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hypnozoite-expressed IESI-1 and IESI-2 proteins suppress schizogony by binding specific RNA motifs
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; expression in P. yoelii blocked schizogony; distinct RNA motif enrichment detected

title: Fmp30p is a mitochondrial phosphatidylinositol hydrolase that modulates CoQ biosynthesis
task: Establish Fmp30p phosphatidylinositol hydrolase role in CoQ biosynthesis regulation
key_results: Fmp30p displays phospholipase D activity toward phosphatidylinositol; FMP30 deletion elevated mitochondrial PI species; elevated PI increased CoQ biosynthesis concomitant with elevated CoQ enzyme expression and enhanced metabolon formation
comments: The discovery of a PI-CoQ biosynthesis link reveals an underappreciated role for lipid composition in controlling mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation.

model_io.model: Yeast FMP30 deletion mutants with purified mitochondria

hypotheses.hypothesis: Fmp30p hydrolysis of PI regulates CoQ biosynthesis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; FMP30 deletion elevated PI and increased CoQ biosynthesis

hypotheses.hypothesis: Elevated mitochondrial PI promotes CoQ metabolon formation
hypotheses.result: Supported; PI elevation correlated with enhanced metabolon assembly

title: Cutaneous gain-of-function mutation of LRIG3 leads to alopecia by upregulation of ERBB, PI3K/AKT, NOTCH1 signaling pathways
task: Elucidate LRIG3 gain-of-function effects on skin homeostasis
key_results: LRIG3 overexpression in transgenic mice caused hair loss and altered skin protein profiles; upregulation of ERBB, PI3K/AKT, and NOTCH1 pathway components; affected keratinocyte differentiation and hair follicle/sebaceous gland markers
comments: The alopecia phenotype is striking but the causal link between pathway upregulation and follicle pathology remains incompletely characterized mechanistically.

hypotheses.hypothesis: LRIG3 overexpression disrupts skin homeostasis by upregulating ERBB, NOTCH, and PI3K/AKT signaling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; transgenic skin showed elevated pathway components and keratinocyte differentiation markers

title: Dupilumab attenuate IL-4 and IL-13 synergistic effect on airway remodeling in asthma via blocking IL-4Rα/STAT6 axis
task: Resolve IL-4/IL-13 synergy in asthmatic airway fibrosis via IL-4Rα/STAT6
key_results: IL-4 and IL-13 synergistically enhanced STAT6 phosphorylation in diseased human lung fibroblasts; upregulated ECM components (collagen I/III, fibronectin) and regulators (MMP-9, TIMP-1/2); dupilumab (IL-4Rα antibody) blocked pro-fibrotic response
comments: The clinical relevance is strong given dupilumab approval, but the specific contribution of IL-4 vs. IL-13 to each ECM component could be better dissected.

model_io.model: Primary human lung fibroblasts (asthmatic vs. normal)

hypotheses.hypothesis: IL-4 and IL-13 act synergistically via IL-4Rα/STAT6 to drive fibroblast pro-fibrotic program
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; combined stimulation synergistically elevated STAT6 phosphorylation and ECM regulators

hypotheses.hypothesis: IL-4Rα blockade prevents cytokine-driven airway remodeling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; dupilumab abrogated IL-4/IL-13-induced pro-fibrotic response

title: Staphylococcus aureus derived extracellular vesicles modulate osteoblast-like cell immune responses independently of vesicle internalization
task: Characterize S. aureus EV-induced immune responses in osteoblasts
key_results: N315 EVs activated TLR2, NF-κB, JAK/STAT, and inflammasome pathways in MG-63 cells; induced IL-8 release and caspase-1 activation; transcriptional response occurred independently of EV internalization
comments: The uncoupling of internalization from transcriptional response is mechanistically intriguing and suggests surface receptor engagement is sufficient.

model_io.model: MG-63 osteoblast-like cells + S. aureus N315 EVs

hypotheses.hypothesis: EVs internalization is required for immune pathway activation
hypotheses.result: Rejected; inhibiting endocytosis did not block transcriptional response

hypotheses.hypothesis: TLR2 surface recognition of EVs suffices to activate immune pathways
hypotheses.result: Supported by data showing pathway induction independent of internalization

title: Kukui nut oil (Aleurites moluccanus seed oil) promotes hair growth by activating the Nrf2/ARE-AKR1C family-PGF2α signaling axis
task: Elucidate Nrf2/ARE-AKR1C-PGF2α axis in hair growth promotion by Kukui nut oil
key_results: Kukui nut oil activated Nrf2 signaling leading to AKR1C family upregulation; elevated PGF2α levels and proliferation markers (Ki67, cyclins B1/D1/E1); human testing confirmed eyelash growth promotion
comments: The mechanistic pathway is well-characterized but the specific bioactive components of Kukui oil driving Nrf2 activation remain incompletely identified.

model_io.model: Ex vivo human hair follicles and human eyelash clinical trial

hypotheses.hypothesis: AMS oil activates Nrf2/ARE signaling to upregulate AKR1C family and PGF2α synthesis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; transcriptional analysis revealed Nrf2 activation and AKR1C upregulation

hypotheses.hypothesis: PGF2α mediates hair growth-promoting effects of AMS oil
hypotheses.result: Supported by elevated PGF2α and proliferation marker induction

title: TLCD1 correlates with malignant progression of hepatocellular carcinoma and activation of the ERK signaling cascade
task: Link TLCD1 overexpression to HCC progression via MAPK/ERK pathway
key_results: TLCD1 upregulated in HCC tissues; high expression associated with shortened overall and disease-free survival; TLCD1 overexpression promoted cell proliferation and metastasis via KRAS/ERK1/2/c-MYC phosphorylation
comments: TLCD1 appears to be a driver rather than passenger, but functional validation of the membrane trafficking role in HCC context is limited.

model_io.model: HCC cell lines with TLCD1 knockdown/overexpression

hypotheses.hypothesis: TLCD1 overexpression activates MAPK/ERK signaling to promote HCC proliferation and metastasis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; TLCD1 upregulation increased phosphorylation of KRAS, ERK1/2, and c-MYC

title: Effects of fluoroquinolone antibiotics on extracellular matrix-related phenotypes in tendon cells
task: Characterize fluoroquinolone-induced ECM phenotypes in tendon cells
key_results: Ciprofloxacin downregulated type I collagen production, assembly capacity, and hydroxyproline content; reduced fibronectin, lysyl oxidase activity, and collagen fibril stiffness/diameter; decreased active β1-integrin expression
comments: The multi-level disruption of collagen biology (synthesis, cross-linking, receptor signaling) provides mechanistic insight into FQ-tendinopathy, though anoikis remains unproven.

model_io.model: Mouse tendon cells treated with ciprofloxacin

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ciprofloxacin disrupts collagen synthesis, cross-linking, and ECM receptor signaling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; ciprofloxacin reduced collagen/fibronectin, lysyl oxidase activity, and β1-integrin

hypotheses.hypothesis: Reduced fibronectin and β1-integrin signaling trigger anoikis in FQ-exposed tenocytes
hypotheses.result: Supported by mechanism but direct anoikis validation not provided

title: Neutrophil extracellular traps offer a new therapeutic target for elephant endotheliotropic herpes virus-hemorrhagic disease (EEHV-HD)
task: Establish neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) pathogenesis in elephant endotheliotropic herpesvirus hemorrhagic disease
key_results: Elephant heterophils release NETs upon stimulation including plasma from sick elephants; tissue samples from fatal cases showed extensive NETs; known NET inhibitors prevented response in vitro
comments: This is the first documentation of NET involvement in EEHV-HD pathology; translating inhibition strategies to elephant medicine will require pharmacokinetic optimization.

model_io.model: Primary elephant heterophils and tissue samples from EEHV-HD cases
inputs: EEHV infection or sick elephant plasma

hypotheses.hypothesis: Uncontrolled NET formation contributes to EEHV-HD pathogenesis
hypotheses.result: Supported; fatal tissue samples showed extensive NETs

hypotheses.hypothesis: NET inhibitors block elephant heterophil NET formation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; known inhibitors prevented response in vitro

title: Integration of donor microbiota following FMT correlates with anti-PD-1 response in melanoma
task: Strain-resolved metagenomic analysis of FMT efficacy in anti-PD-1 melanoma therapy
key_results: Therapeutic benefit linked to donor microbiota integration (not diversity alone); responders acquired more donor strains, maintained stable microbiomes, enriched metabolic/communication functions; non-responders showed taxonomic instability and pathogen-associated genes
comments: Novel strain-resolved approach; meta-analysis across three trials (n=41) strengthens findings; mechanistic link to tumor immune profiles supported but causality not established.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Successful donor strain integration predicts anti-PD-1 response
hypotheses.result: Responders showed greater post-FMT donor similarity, more donor strains, stable microbiomes vs. non-responders

hypotheses.hypothesis: Microbiome stability and metabolic capacity drive immunotherapy efficacy
hypotheses.result: Responders enriched for community-level metabolism/communication; non-responders show taxonomic instability and pathogen-associated secretion systems

title: Pan-cancer single-cell atlases of mouse and human tumor-associated dendritic cells
task: Pan-cancer single-cell atlases of tumor-associated dendritic cell subsets and states
key_results: Mapped DC subsets/states across 14 mouse tumor models and 10 human cancer types; TADCs conserved between species; favorable survival linked to specific DC phenotypes
comments: Comprehensive multi-species comparison; mouse-human translation validated but species-specific differences noted, limiting direct clinical extrapolation.

inputs: single-cell transcriptomes from mouse and human tumors

hypotheses.hypothesis: Tumor-associated DCs acquire distinct inflammatory states during progression
hypotheses.result: TADCs show inflammatory phenotype with tumor progression; lymph node DCs also reprogrammed

hypotheses.hypothesis: DC phenotype associates with anti-tumor immunity and patient survival
hypotheses.result: Specific TADC clusters linked to differential survival outcomes in human cohorts

title: Structure-based screening and a conformational biosensor identify a GPR183 inverse agonist and an activation switch
task: AI-driven virtual screening and conformational biosensor validation of GPR183 inverse agonist
key_results: Compound 78 potently inhibits Gi signaling and β-arrestin2 recruitment; blocks agonist-driven PBMC migration ex vivo; Y260 (TM6) identified as activation switch; molecular dynamics/mutagenesis confirmed binding mode
comments: Excellent integration of computational screening, biophysical assays, and functional validation; limited to single candidate compound and ex vivo validation—in vivo efficacy and selectivity unknown.

inputs: 70 compounds from initial screen, expanded hit series
outputs: ranked compounds by predicted binding affinity

hypotheses.hypothesis: Compound 78 selectively inhibits GPR183 signaling via core receptor binding
hypotheses.result: Potent Gi and β-arrestin2 inhibition; mutagenesis confirmed Y260 binding interaction

hypotheses.hypothesis: Y260 in TM6 is a molecular switch for GPR183 activation
hypotheses.result: Mutation alters compound efficacy and induces signaling bias; critical for activation mechanism

title: Multikingdom microbiome-based machine learning enables multiple sclerosis diagnosis
task: Multikingdom microbiome-based ML diagnosis of multiple sclerosis
key_results: Discovery cohort: 90 bacterial, 3 fungal, 2 viral species; ML models achieved AUC 0.977–0.978 internally; external validation AUC 0.813–0.849 (30-marker models)
comments: Strong multimodal integration and external validation; performance drop on external cohorts (0.977→0.813) highlights generalization challenges.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multikingdom microbiome features improve MS diagnosis over bacteria alone
hypotheses.result: Full model AUC 0.977–0.978; external validation 0.813–0.849 with 30-marker subset

hypotheses.hypothesis: Faecalibacterium spp. and L-methionine biosynthesis associate with MS protection
hypotheses.result: Both less abundant in MS patients; identified as key predictors

title: Prostate cancer detection using modified transformer with optimal feature selection from MRI images
task: Automated prostate cancer detection from MRI using modified transformer
key_results: ProstateNet framework integrates bilateral filtering, RRM feature extraction, ISBO optimization, and modified transformer; specific performance metrics not quantified in abstract
comments: Architecture description lacks concrete validation metrics; claims of superiority to baselines are not substantiated with numerical results.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Modified transformer with CapsuleNet (vs. FFN) improves cancer detection accuracy
hypotheses.result: Approach proposed as promising but specific performance metrics not reported

title: A new scheme for knee joint CT image segmentation: A max-flow and watershed method driving semi-automatic CT knee bone segmentation
task: Semi-automated 3D CT knee joint segmentation via max-flow and watershed
key_results: Proposed method outperformed four open-source tools on 18 datasets in precision, sensitivity, and specificity; computational efficiency and reduced manual effort achieved
comments: Small validation set (n=18); lack of quantitative comparison metrics (e.g., Dice coefficient) limits assessment against state-of-the-art.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adaptive weighted max-flow captures ill-defined edges in knee CT better than standard methods
hypotheses.result: Higher precision, sensitivity, specificity vs. four open-source tools on 18 real datasets

title: Long-term continuous monitoring of wearable ECG signals for atrial fibrillation detection
task: Lightweight CNN for atrial fibrillation detection from long-term wearable ECG
key_results: Fine-tuned model on TRAdA cohort (Phase 2, n=117): specificity 0.971, F1 0.891, AUC 0.992, accuracy 0.969; superior to original model (specificity 0.914, AUC 0.988); validated on InCorDB, CODE15
comments: Domain adaptation (fine-tuning on wearable data) substantially improved performance; reasonable specificity/sensitivity balance; external validation on three datasets supports generalization.

model_io.model: Lightweight CNN (trained on CinC2021, fine-tuned on TRAdA)
inputs: long-term wearable ECG recordings (24h to 7 days)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Domain adaptive fine-tuning on wearable ECG improves AFib detection
hypotheses.result: Phase 2 (7-day): fine-tuned specificity 0.971, AUC 0.992 vs. original 0.914, 0.988

hypotheses.hypothesis: Lightweight CNNs generalize across independent ECG cohorts (InCorDB, CODE15, TRAdA)
hypotheses.result: Multi-cohort validation supports real-world applicability in ambulatory settings

title: Machine learning-based screening model for Tic disorders comorbid with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder in children and SHAP value interpretation: a retrospective observational study
task: ML-based screening for ADHD comorbidity in children with tic disorders
key_results: Random forest model: AUC 0.780, accuracy 0.793, recall 0.793, F1 0.753 on test set; seven key features identified; learning initiative and guardian type were top predictors (SHAP)
comments: Solid feature selection and SHAP interpretability; single-center retrospective study without external validation severely limits clinical implementation; model calibration adequate (Brier 0.18).

inputs: 28 clinical features: demographics, family factors, academic/emotional/sleep metrics

hypotheses.hypothesis: Seven features (learning initiative, guardian type, etc.) capture ADHD comorbidity risk in TD
hypotheses.result: Random forest: AUC 0.780, accuracy 0.793; learning initiative (SHAP 0.07) and guardian type (0.05) most influential

hypotheses.hypothesis: ML screening improves early identification of TD+ADHD comorbidity
hypotheses.result: Model achieves reasonable discrimination; external validation required before clinical use

title: Conserved mRNA expression patterns of the Klotho family in canine mammary tumors and human breast cancer
task: Comparative mRNA expression of Klotho family in canine and human breast tumors
key_results: αKlotho and βKlotho reduced in CMTs; γKlotho increased (>65% of TNBC); 52 genes dysregulated similarly in human/canine datasets; enriched AR, VEGF, ERK signaling pathways
comments: Good species conservation validation; functional role of γKlotho remains speculative; larger CMT cohort and mechanistic studies needed.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Klotho expression patterns are conserved between canine and human breast tumors
hypotheses.result: αKlotho/βKlotho reduced; γKlotho elevated in both species, especially TNBC

hypotheses.hypothesis: γKlotho acts as oncogene via AR, VEGF, ERK pathways
hypotheses.result: 52 dysregulated genes enriched in these pathways; γKlotho-high tumors more aggressive

title: A lightweight deep learning model with channel attention for kidney cell classification from microscopy images
task: Lightweight CNN with channel attention for kidney cell classification from microscopy
key_results: CytoECA-Net: 75.56% accuracy (TissueMNIST, 236k images), AUC 0.9564; 97.76% on KMC-RENAL dataset; 1.7M parameters, 2.43 ms inference time per image
comments: Excellent parameter efficiency and inference speed; modest accuracy on TissueMNIST (75.56%) suggests room for architectural improvement, but strong performance on histopathology dataset.
